summary: Root-caused the false 'Working offline' banner: the CrmEngineFreshness store (crm/store/index.ts) that drives the banner/chip on Home, Today, and household pages defaults to {kind:'offline'} at module load and is only ever updated by CrmSyncEngine.bootstrap()/.stop() — a class that is NEVER instantiated anywhere in the running app (only in its own unit test, SyncEngine.test.ts). The real production CRM delivery path is liveRecordRelay.ts, built on MatterDocSyncClient/MatterSyncClient, which already exposes a purpose-built onStatus callback ('Status changes — drives the UI badge', per its own doc comment) that was simply never wired up. Net effect: the freshness store was permanently stuck on its 'offline' default from app start, completely disconnected from real connectivity (including the Cloud AI path, which is a separate mechanism entirely) — exactly matching both benches' observation that the banner showed while Cloud AI requests were demonstrably succeeding. Fix: liveRecordRelay.ts now passes an onStatus callback into MatterDocSyncClient that maps the real SyncStatus ('connecting'/'catching-up' -> syncing, 'live' -> live, 'offline'/'idle' -> offline, 'error' -> error) into setCrmEngineFreshness(), and stopLiveRecordRelay() now honestly resets freshness to 'offline' when delivery actually stops (previously it left the last live/syncing state stranded). Semantic decided: 'Working offline' means CRM record delivery relay connectivity specifically (matches the banner's own copy, 'delivery waits until you reconnect'), not general network or AI-provider reachability -- this was already implied by the code's own onStatus hook and its doc comment, so it was not an ambiguous call.

driven_live: Not driven in the packaged/dev Tauri UI (never launched the app window). Verified at the code/test boundary instead: a new regression test (liveRecordRelay.freshness.test.ts) exercises the real production wiring path end-to-end -- ensureLiveRecordRelay() -> the real build()/stopLiveRecordRelay() logic in liveRecordRelay.ts -> the real onStatus callback now wired into MatterDocSyncClient -> setCrmEngineFreshness() -> the same store the banner/chip reads. Only the outermost transport (MatterDocSyncClient's internal WebSocket/HTTP calls) is mocked, since a unit-test environment has no live relay server; everything from the relay boundary inward is real code, not reimplemented or stubbed logic. Confirmed by reverting the fix (git stash) and re-running the same test: both assertions fail exactly as the bug predicts (freshness stays {kind:'offline'} even after the relay signals 'live'); restoring the fix makes them pass.
assumptions: Decided the 'Working offline' semantic is CRM record delivery relay connectivity (not general network reachability, not AI-provider reachability). This was not actually ambiguous: the banner's own copy says '...delivery waits until you reconnect', and the transport layer (MatterSyncClient) already had a purpose-built onStatus callback whose own doc comment says 'Status changes — drives the UI badge' -- the intent was already encoded in the code, it was just never connected.

When there is no shared/firm matter for the current workspace (useLiveCrmRecords sees no sharedMatterId), no relay session is ever started and freshness correctly stays at its honest 'offline' default -- this matches an existing, intentionally-written test (CrmHome.test.tsx: 'keeps the default Home honest with the real offline engine state') which this fix does not change or break.

CrmSyncEngine (the class the freshness store's doc comment nominally attributes freshness updates to) is confirmed genuinely dead code in production -- grepped the whole repo; it is only ever instantiated in its own unit test (SyncEngine.test.ts). Left it untouched (out of scope for this fix; the brief's exclusion list didn't cover it but rewriting/removing unrelated dead code beyond the fix's boundary was not requested).

Symlinked node_modules (root and intake-page/) from /home/jameson/lane-combined-merge per the brief's setup instructions, after confirming both package-lock.json files are byte-identical. Also had to copy (not symlink) src-tauri/binaries/* (gitignored sidecar binaries: piper, llama.cpp libs, etc.) from the same source tree, since git worktrees don't carry gitignored files and cargo build needs them present -- copied rather than symlinked specifically so it wouldn't disturb the tracked .gitkeep placeholder and would never show up as a spurious git change.
remaining_risks: `cargo test --workspace --locked` (the Rust half of the mandated full gate) never completed a run to a pass/fail result. Made 6 total genuine attempts (3 full `npm run gate` runs, 2 standalone `cargo test` runs, plus separately verifying `tsc --noEmit` in isolation) over roughly 30 minutes, including waiting for a competing lantern-plus lane's own gate run to fully exit before retrying. Every attempt was killed by SIGTERM mid-compile, never by a real compiler/test failure -- the partial compile output before each kill showed zero errors across the hundreds of dependency crates that did build. Root cause is confirmed environmental, not this diff: `systemctl status user-1000.slice` showed the box's shared 52G memory cgroup repeatedly bottoming out to under 5G (once to 36MB) available, independent of which stage my own job was at; a concurrent, unrelated lane (wt-sidebar-blank) was observed running its own live `tsc` process consuming 1.4GB+ RAM during my final attempt; and the box's earlyoom safety daemon is explicitly configured with `--prefer ^(rustc|cargo|cc1plus|cc1|collect2|vitest|esbuild|tsc)$` -- i.e. it is deliberately tuned to sacrifice exactly these process names first under memory pressure, which is precisely what kept happening to my cargo/tsc jobs. This fix touches zero files under src-tauri/ (Rust), so a Rust-side regression from this specific change is very unlikely, but it is honestly unconfirmed -- acceptance_met is set to false for exactly this reason.

Every OTHER gate stage was independently verified passing on this branch: full `npx vitest run` (933 test files / 8108 tests, including the 2 new regression tests, 0 failures), `npm run lint:gate` (clean, 0 regressions after fixing one require-await finding in my own new test file), permanent-handle guard, design-token leak guard, Tauri version parity check, Tauri TS/Rust command contract check, the intake wire-contract suite (bun test), provider-front-door check, consent-gate wiring check, case-only filename collision check, and `tsc --noEmit` typecheck (run standalone, exit 0, separate from the contested composite gate run).
